name: Heavens to Betsy
label: Kill Rock Stars
lede: Two friends from Eugene, one $100 drum kit, and a first show at the International Pop Underground Convention before they had written much of a set.

eras.title: A train to Athens, a bluff in Olympia
eras.text: Corin Tucker and Tracy Sawyer met in middle school in Eugene, Oregon. Before either had a real band, they took a train to Athens, Georgia; a year later Tucker was at Evergreen in Olympia and the duo was on a festival bill.

years.cap: Tucker and Sawyer, early days. Credit to be added.
years.h: Corin Tucker and Tracy Sawyer take a train to Athens, Georgia
years.p: Before Sawyer's senior year and Tucker's freshman year, the friends made a pilgrimage to Georgia. Sawyer came home with a used drum kit, possibly for $100.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Tucker had already come up with the name Heavens to Betsy that spring. Tucker's father gave her a handmade guitar and amp, and the two practiced at her parents' house.

In the 2018 Bandcamp Daily interview, the pair say they met the band Earthworms in Athens and picked up drum kit parts there.

years.h: First show: Girl Night at the International Pop Underground Convention
years.p: KAOS radio's Michelle Noel asked Tucker to play International Pop Underground Convention Girl Night, and she said yes. They played three songs on opening night, called Love Rock Revolution Girl Style Now.
years.xp:
The K Records festival in Olympia opened with an all-female bill that is often cited as a turning point for riot grrrl. Heavens to Betsy played a three-song set, per Wikipedia.

Tucker told Bandcamp Daily she wasn't sure they had even written a song yet.

eras.title: Walkie-talkies, Calculated, and the end
eras.text: The Olympia community put out their records and they toured in two cars linked by walkie-talkies. The one full-length arrived just before the band ended in mid-1994, and Tucker's next band followed within months.

years.h: Eight-song demo tape, recorded by Molly Neuman, on K Records
years.p: [[Bratmobile|d6dfbc0b-d737-49df-be8e-517b85985bcb]] drummer Molly Neuman recorded it at Evergreen. According to Wikipedia the master is missing, so it has never been reissued.

years.h: Split 7-inch with Bratmobile: "My Secret" on K Records
years.p: The two Olympia duos share a single on K Records, the label that had given them their first stage.

years.h: These Monsters Are Real on Kill Rock Stars
years.p: Their four-song 7-inch for Kill Rock Stars. It was remastered and reissued in 2018.
years.xp: Sources differ on the year: Wikipedia and Trouser Press say 1992, while the Bandcamp Daily piece says 1993.

years.h: Bellingham show: Tucker meets Carrie Brownstein
years.p: A show in Bellingham, Washington introduced Tucker to [[Carrie Brownstein|2b7d41d8-21d4-4410-a57b-5ddaeb131094]] of Western Washington University, who was then in [[Excuse 17|bad37a2a-1ab8-4605-b8f3-e0615cd7de64]].

years.cap: On tour. Credit to be added.
years.h: Two-car convoy, walkie-talkies and a trip to England
years.p: They toured the US with [[Bratmobile|d6dfbc0b-d737-49df-be8e-517b85985bcb]], with the cars linked by walkie-talkies, then played in England.
years.xp: Wikipedia says there was also a later national tour with Brownstein's [[Excuse 17|bad37a2a-1ab8-4605-b8f3-e0615cd7de64]]. In the Bandcamp Daily interview the band describes booking shows before the internet by phoning venues and taking down handwritten directions.

years.h: Recording Calculated in Seattle with John Goodmanson
years.p: Four days in Seattle with engineer John Goodmanson, with the band producing itself.
Twelve songs, 39 minutes 50 seconds, including "Axemen" and "Waitress Hell". Robert Christgau gave it an A minus.
years.xp:
Tucker plays guitar and sings, Sawyer drums and plays bass. Trouser Press said it showed anger, fear, confusion and vulnerability despite basic instrumental skills, with Tucker's wail set against Sawyer's screams.

Trouser Press dates the album to 1993. Wikipedia gives March 21, 1994.

years.cap: Heavens to Betsy, live. Credit to be added.
years.p: Tucker and Sawyer said the band ended as their friendship and the seriousness of the music started to pull apart.
years.xp:
They put it down to changing relationships and personalities, and to not having the maturity or communication skills for a business partnership at their age.

Wikipedia lists Tucker's later bands as [[Sleater-Kinney|e36e78eb-3ace-4acd-882c-16789e700ab7]], Heartless Martin, Cadallaca, the Corin Tucker Band and Filthy Friends, and Sawyer's as Flying Tigers, The Lies and Motel No-Tell.

years.h: Tucker starts Sleater-Kinney with Carrie Brownstein
years.p: The new band was [[Sleater-Kinney|e36e78eb-3ace-4acd-882c-16789e700ab7]]; Trouser Press names Lora Macfarlane as its first drummer.

eras.title: Back after 32 years
eras.text: The band's songs later turned up in films and the video game Gone Home. In 2026 the duo played again.

years.cap: Reunion show, Turn! Turn! Turn!, Portland. Credit to be added.
years.h: Secret reunion show in Portland after 32 years
years.p: Tucker and Sawyer played 18 songs at Turn! Turn! Turn!, including "Calculated" and "Axemen". A 10-date US tour starting October 17 in San Francisco followed.
years.xp: Stereogum reported the show was announced the day after. The tour was set for October and November 2026, with tickets going on sale July 2.

sources.title: Bandcamp Daily: A Chat with Corin Tucker and Tracy Sawyer
